intro.headline: GLOBAL AI INTELLIGENCE WIRE
intro.script: Breaking today: China blocks SoftBank's 5.4 billion dollars takeover of ABB's robotics division: FT. From the SanMitra Newsroom, this is the Daily AI Brief for 05 November 2026.

stories.headline: China blocks SoftBank's 5.4 billion dollars takeover of ABB's robotics division: FT
stories.script: Our lead story today. Softbank had agreed to buy ABB's robotics business in October last year, as CEO Masayoshi Son sought to establish SoftBank as a core player in the development of artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Google unveils 15 billion dollars data centre investment in Malaysia
stories.script: Turning to the United States. Google said on Wednesday it will spend 15 billion dollars in Malaysia on data centres and other infrastructure, according to The Economic Times. The company said the money will be invested over the next two years, from 2027 to 2028, as demand for artificial intelligence services surges. The new commitment builds on a 2 billion dollars investment Google announced in 2024.
stories.whyThisMatters: Google said on Wednesday it will spend $15 billion in Malaysia on data centres and other infrastructure, according to The Economic Times.
keyPoints: Google unveils 15 billion dollars data centre investment in Malaysia
The Economic Times

stories.headline: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
stories.script: In other news. Meta has bought Conductor, an AI coding startup founded in 2024, Tech in Asia reports. Meta confirmed the deal on November 4 as it broadens its AI coding tools.
stories.whyThisMatters: Meta has bought Conductor, an AI coding startup founded in 2024, Tech in Asia reports.
keyPoints: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
Tech in Asia

stories.headline: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights
stories.script: In China. Moonshot AI has published the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, TechNode reports, so organisations can now run the company's flagship multimodal model on their own. The model uses a mixture-of-experts design, with 2.8 trillion parameters in total and roughly 104 billion active for each inference. It can handle a context window of about one million tokens. Compared with Kimi K3, the new version adds more reinforcement learning aimed at coding, 3D creation, financial research and lengthy agent tasks. The model was previously offered only through Kimi's apps and API. Huawei said it will support inference through vLLM Ascend and SGLang on its Atlas A3 and Ascend 950 systems.
stories.whyThisMatters: Moonshot AI has published the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, TechNode reports, so organisations can now run the company's flagship multimodal model on their own.
keyPoints: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights

stories.script: In Asia. Reap and Meitu's EveLab Insight are exploring AI-driven beauty shopping, Tech in Asia reports. Reap said its service lets AI agents make card payments within limits users have approved.
stories.whyThisMatters: Reap and Meitu's EveLab Insight are exploring AI-driven beauty shopping, Tech in Asia reports.

stories.headline: AI sharpens cat-and-mouse hacking battle as companies strengthen defences
stories.script: Turning to India. Companies around the world are confronting a surge of cyber threats that executives say artificial intelligence is speeding up, according to The Economic Times. Recent incidents range from hacked supermarket fridges to a record cryptocurrency theft at Binance and an emergency over flaws in popular web software.
stories.whyThisMatters: Companies around the world are confronting a surge of cyber threats that executives say artificial intelligence is speeding up, according to The Economic Times.
keyPoints: AI sharpens cat-and-mouse hacking battle as companies strengthen defences
The Economic Times

stories.headline: Activists across Europe prepare two days of protests against datacentres
stories.script: Around the world. Campaigners across Europe are getting ready for two days of demonstrations against datacentres, The Guardian reports. More than 100 groups in 15 countries are coordinating the action, which takes place on Friday and Saturday under the name Stop Dirty Data Centres. The groups want a halt to major artificial intelligence projects and are pressing for a moratorium on large datacentre developments. They point to environmental and social burdens, describing them as costs that "we can no longer afford".
stories.whyThisMatters: Campaigners across Europe are getting ready for two days of demonstrations against datacentres, The Guardian reports.
keyPoints: Activists across Europe prepare two days of protests against datacentres
The Guardian

stories.headline: Nothing plans December launch for first AI-native device
stories.script: In China. Nothing will release its first AI-native hardware product in December, founder and chief executive Carl Pei said on November 4, according to TechNode. Pei called the device a screenless productivity tool and said an app on its own could not have provided what it does. In an essay called Toolmakers, he argued that AI tools miss much of the context around people's work, such as conversations and ideas that never get typed into a chatbot. He suggested ordinary hardware could help fill that gap. The company has not revealed the device's exact form, specifications or price.
stories.whyThisMatters: Nothing will release its first AI-native hardware product in December, founder and chief executive Carl Pei said on November 4, according to TechNode.
keyPoints: Nothing plans December launch for first AI-native device
TechNode

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi Hosted Agents as a Managed Agent-Harness Cloud Service
stories.script: Elsewhere. Moonshot AI has launched Kimi Hosted Agents, a managed cloud service that runs AI agents around the clock, Pandaily reports. It includes sandboxes, audit trails, an Inference Hook and eight finance templates, sparing teams from hosting the runtime themselves.
stories.whyThisMatters: Moonshot AI has launched Kimi Hosted Agents, a managed cloud service that runs AI agents around the clock, Pandaily reports.

stories.headline: UK found to be ‘dangerously’ reliant on China for critical minerals needed for defence and AI
stories.script: Also today. A parliamentary inquiry has concluded that Britain relies on China to a dangerous degree for critical raw materials, The Guardian reports. Members of the business select committee said these materials are essential for the military, renewable energy infrastructure and artificial intelligence, and warned that reaching net zero is also under threat. The MPs urged an urgent, centralised policy. They also proposed a critical minerals finance facility to help pay for rare earth and other critical mineral mines, using grants, equity and debt to speed up efforts to diversify supply.
stories.whyThisMatters: A parliamentary inquiry has concluded that Britain relies on China to a dangerous degree for critical raw materials, The Guardian reports.

stories.headline: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
stories.script: From the research desk. Researchers are rethinking how robots turn sight into movement in a paper titled From Pixels to Actions, Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies. These models combine camera images, written instructions and physical actions. Usually a separate visual encoder first condenses an image into a summary, and only then does the system reason about what to do. The researchers argue this can discard the details that handling objects depends on, such as edges, depth, shape and small changes. Their system, NEO-VLA, drops the separate encoder. Light processing layers break images into pieces that are handled together with language, letting the action component draw on visual information at several stages.
stories.whyThisMatters: Researchers are rethinking how robots turn sight into movement in a paper titled From Pixels to Actions, Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies.
keyPoints: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
